title: Adjectives of the Third Declension
subtitle: ἀληθής, εὐδαίμων, πᾶς — mixed and pure third-declension adjectives.
objectives: Decline third-declension adjectives of two and three terminations.
Recognize mixed declension adjectives (third in masculine/neuter, first in feminine).
Decline the irregular adjective πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν (all, every).
Use third-declension adjectives in attributive and predicate position.

sections.heading: Third-declension adjectives
sections.body:
Some adjectives follow the third declension. Two-termination adjectives have one form for masculine and feminine, another for neuter. Three-termination adjectives have separate forms for all three genders.

Many third-declension adjectives are mixed: third declension in the masculine and neuter, first declension in the feminine. ἀληθής (true) is a two-termination adjective. εὐδαίμων (happy, fortunate) is a mixed three-termination adjective.

sections.heading: Two-termination: ἀληθής (true)
sections.body:
Masculine and feminine:
              singular        plural
  nominative  ἀληθής          ἀληθεῖς
  genitive    ἀληθοῦς         ἀληθῶν
  dative      ἀληθεῖ          ἀληθέσι(ν)
  accusative  ἀληθῆ           ἀληθεῖς
  vocative    ἀληθές          ἀληθεῖς

Neuter:
              singular        plural
  nominative  ἀληθές          ἀληθῆ
  genitive    ἀληθοῦς         ἀληθῶν
  dative      ἀληθεῖ          ἀληθέσι(ν)
  accusative  ἀληθές          ἀληθῆ
  vocative    ἀληθές          ἀληθῆ

This follows the εσ-stem pattern with contraction.

sections.heading: Mixed declension: εὐδαίμων (happy, fortunate)
sections.body:
Masculine and feminine follow the third declension consonant-stem pattern (stem εὐδαιμον-). Feminine can also use first-declension forms in some dialects.

              singular        plural
  nominative  εὐδαίμων        εὐδαίμονες
  genitive    εὐδαίμονος      εὐδαιμόνων
  dative      εὐδαίμονι       εὐδαίμοσι(ν)
  accusative  εὐδαίμονα       εὐδαίμονας

Neuter singular nominative/accusative: εὔδαιμον.

sections.heading: Irregular: πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν (all, every)
sections.body:
Masculine:
              singular        plural
  nominative  πᾶς             πάντες
  genitive    παντός          πάντων
  dative      παντί           πᾶσι(ν)
  accusative  πάντα           πάντας

Feminine (first declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  πᾶσα            πᾶσαι
  genitive    πάσης           πασῶν
  dative      πάσῃ            πάσαις
  accusative  πᾶσαν           πάσας

Neuter:
              singular        plural
  nominative  πᾶν             πάντα
  genitive    παντός          πάντων
  dative      παντί           πᾶσι(ν)
  accusative  πᾶν             πάντα

The stem is παντ-. The nominative singular masculine and neuter drop the τ.

items.answer: genitive singular masculine or neuter of πᾶς
One form for masculine and feminine, another for neuter.
Third declension in masculine/neuter, first declension in feminine.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.10 introduces the present participle active. The participle is a verbal adjective: it has tense and voice like a verb, but it declines like an adjective. λύων means 'loosing' — the one who is loosing.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can decline ἀληθής and πᾶς from memory and can recognize third-declension adjectives in Greek sentences.
